Write scenarios by hand

Source: R/scenario.R
step.Rd

A scenario is a sequence of steps run in one environment, so later steps see the objects earlier steps created. Use scenario files for code the vignettes do not cover, or for vignettes that cannot simply run. Each step's code is kept exactly as written and run unchanged under both versions.

Usage

step(
  id,
  kind = c("run", "setup", "fit", "print", "plot"),
  expr,
  label = id,
  values = FALSE,
  time = NULL,
  w = 7,
  h = 4.5
)

scenario(id, ..., title = id, source = "")

Arguments

id

Identifier: unique within its scenario (steps) or the dossier (scenarios).

kind

Kind of step, see Details.

expr

Code of the step, unevaluated. Wrap several lines in { }: each top-level expression inside runs as if typed at the console.

label

Label shown in the report.

values

Collect numbers and element names (see Details).

time

Time the step with repeats. Defaults to TRUE for "fit" steps.

w, h

Figure size in inches for plots the step draws.

...

Steps (scenario()).

title, source

Title of the scenario and where its code comes from, shown in the report.

Value

step(): an pkgdossier_step; scenario(): an pkgdossier_scenario.

Details

Kinds of step:

  • "setup": run, not reported (data preparation).

  • "run": run and reported (console output, warnings, errors, plots).

  • "fit": like "run", and timed with repeats.

  • "print": the visible value is printed and its printed form compared on its own.

  • "plot": drawn to PNG at w x h inches.

Every step captures console output, warnings, errors and plots whatever its kind. With values = TRUE the step also collects every number and short string inside its visible value, and inside any object it assigns at top level, keyed by path, plus the element names a user's code might read (x$foo$bar).

Examples

scenario("basics", title = "Linear model", source = "README",
  step("setup", "setup", d <- head(mtcars, 20)),
  step("fit", "fit", fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = d)),
  step("coef", "print", coef(fit), values = TRUE),
  step("plot", "plot", plot(d$wt, d$mpg), w = 5, h = 4)
)
#> <pkgdossier scenario> basics: Linear model (4 steps)
#>   setup                    setup 
#>   fit                      fit   
#>   coef                     print 
#>   plot                     plot
